title: Big Brains, Tiny Board: Pupavision, an Agentic Physical AI Instrument for Monitoring Drosophila Pupariation and Lifecycle Transitions
abstract: arXiv:2611.22136v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many biology experiments are limited by the availability and ease of use of instruments that monitor and record them. For example, the timing of pupariation in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, a widely used model organism, can provide biologically relevant information about growth regulation and is often recorded manually. Here, we present Pupavision, a small physical AI instrument built from a single-board Linux computer and a day/night camera for roughly 45 to 75 US dollars in parts. The key idea is that a frontier coding agent runs its agentic harness directly on the tiny board. The model thinks in the cloud, but the agent works on the device. The agent assists image capture, writes code to repair errors, and checks the experiment every day to keep raw data capture reliable. tldr: Pupavision以约45–75美元的成本将前沿编程智能体直接部署在单板计算机上，使其自主完成果蝇蛹化等生命周期实验的图像采集、错误修复与日常检查，实现了低成本、高可靠性的自动化生物学实验监测。
en_tdlr: Pupavision is a $45–75 physical AI instrument that runs a frontier coding agent directly on a tiny single-board computer to autonomously handle image capture, error repair, and daily experiment checks for monitoring Drosophila pupariation and lifecycle transitions.
